case.pattern_description: A coordinated device-spoofing campaign utilizes a specific Samsung SM-G935F Android device profile behind anonymous IP proxies to conduct unauthorized online purchases across dozens of unrelated debit cards. The perpetrators maintain low individual transaction amounts ($70 to $115) and space transactions across days to evade statistical model thresholds. This exact device profile and behavioral signature were previously investigated and confirmed as an undocumented typology across closed cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035.

Card C13487-K1's prior history consists of 69 out of 71 in-person retail charges (product W), making two online purchases of product C totaling $187.33 from a brand-new holder profile anomalous.
On 2016-11-22, in-person retail purchase 3478886 occurred in region 272 at 18:04:15, less than two hours after online transaction 3478561 in region 191 at 16:11:00.
Flagged transaction 3478561 received a low fraud model score of 0.006 with a calibrated historical fraud rate of 0.006, and legacy risk score of 0.05.
The transaction billing region 191 is consistent with card C13487-K1's frequent billing history (36 of 71 prior transactions), and region 191 carries a low fraud lift of 0.05.

When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

case.summary: An analyst-initiated review of transaction 3478561 ($74.96) on card C13487-K1 identified an unauthorized online purchase linked to a coordinated device-spoofing campaign. The charge, along with a preceding transaction of $112.37 on 2016-11-15, was initiated from device D004630 (Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge SM-G935F) through an anonymous IP proxy. Knowledge graph analysis established that device D004630 anchors fraud ring 36700632, links to 21 distinct cards in the active 30-day window, and is tied to four prior confirmed-fraud cases. In contrast, card C13487-K1's established baseline consists almost entirely of in-person retail activity, with a legitimate physical transaction occurring in region 272 shortly after the flagged online charge. Card C13487-K1 was confirmed compromised under an undocumented typology, resulting in card blocking, SAR filing, and monitoring of connected accounts.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an undocumented, coordinated device-spoofing fraud campaign affecting customer C13487 and card C13487-K1. Between November 15, 2016, and November 22, 2016, two unauthorized card-not-present online purchases totaling $187.33 were executed against the account. Specifically, transaction 3460634 for $112.37 was processed on November 15, 2016, at 20:30:00, followed by transaction 3478561 for $74.96 on November 22, 2016, at 16:11:00. Both online transactions were billed in region 191 from device D004630, identified as a Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge SM-G935F running Android 7.0 and Chrome 62.0. The actor routed the transactions through an anonymous IP proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS), registering device D004630 as a new device for the card. Graph analysis confirmed that device D004630 is a central pivot anchoring fraud ring 36700632, directly connecting 21 distinct cards within a 30-day window under identical anonymous proxy configurations. Device D004630 is also directly linked to four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035) involving unauthorized online card abuse. This unauthorized online activity sharply diverges from the customer's historical profile, which consists of 69 in-person retail transactions out of 71 prior transactions. Furthermore, a legitimate in-person retail charge occurred in region 272 less than two hours after online transaction 3478561, confirming conflicting physical locations. The bank has blocked card C13487-K1 to prevent further losses, placed 20 connected cards under active monitoring, and escalated the broader fraud ring for remediation.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.94 (exceeding the 0.85 threshold) supported by multiple independent incriminating bases, including decisive cross-card links to a known fraud ring, strong device proxy anomalies, four confirmed prior fraud cases, and substantial departure from the cardholder's baseline.
